# Julian Jakob

> Julian Jakob is an Austrian brand designer based in Salzburg who develops brand concepts and visual systems with meaning and depth — finding the conceptual way into a brand and building the system that carries it across every touchpoint. He has worked on identities and campaigns for Spotify, Meta, Sony Music and Red Bull Music, as well as work for Alto New York (with Studio Herrström) that won multiple awards, including Cannes Lions. Website: https://julianjakob.at

Julian works as a digital brand designer at LOOP (https://www.agentur-loop.com/), where he develops visual systems and the concepts and visual direction for pitches. He occasionally takes on independent projects. He presents his full portfolio in person or on a call rather than as public case studies; the website shows a feed of project snapshots with his role on each.

## Career

- LOOP — Digital Brand Designer (since 2026): brand design and visual systems; concepts and visual direction for pitches. Clients include Porsche, Amazon Prime and PrimaLoft. Team page: https://www.agentur-loop.com/about
- Studio Herrström — Junior Designer (2024–2026): concepting and design for clients including Spotify, Meta, Sony Music and Red Bull Music, and for Alto New York (award-winning work, including Cannes Lions); presented creative work to stakeholders. https://www.studioherrstrom.com/about
- Independent projects (since 2022): occasional brand and visual-system work for selected companies and individuals.
- Education: Graphic & Information Design at New Design University (NDU), St. Pölten (2021–2024), specialising in Integrated Campaigns and Brand Design, graduated with excellence; Erasmus exchange at ESADA, Spain (2022–2023); Handelsakademie (business school) Matura (2015–2020).

## Approach

Most brand problems are clarity problems, not design problems. Every project follows four steps:

1. Research — stakeholder workshops, competitive analysis and audience analysis to define what is needed and why.
2. Construct — positioning, brand strategy and messaging translated into a clear brand architecture.
3. Deliver — naming, visual identity and design system, whether launching or evolving a brand.
4. Implement — campaigns, digital applications and editorial design that carry the identity consistently.

A brand system is built as a team: Julian works closely with specialists in strategy, copy, motion design and development, and stays involved with a system after launch.
